items.text: – Da, kupit ću ti vejiku lutkicu. Kad mi dođe novac, kupit ću ti i bolju od te, Babina djevojčice.
items.q: A stranger on the street answers his little girl, playfully copying her baby talk. Does that come through?
before: – Viiiž, Baba, Baba, kupiš mi ovu vejiku lutkicu?

items.text: Kažem, ako samo sjediš ovdje i čitaš poeziju, nikakav ti se kruh neće ugrijati.
items.q: A friend criticises Amir for reading poetry all day. A Persian expression kept word for word: can you guess its meaning?
Maman quotes a lonely friend who has nothing to do all day. A Persian saying kept word for word: can you guess its meaning?

items.text: Smijući se, Hooman me snažno lupi po leđima i kocka šećera mi skoči u grlo.
items.q: Hooman thumps Amir on the back while he drinks tea. A Persian image kept word for word: can you guess what happens?

items.text: Nemoj reći onom jadnom Eskandaru, inače će nas posaditi još sat vremena i moralizirati i jelo će mi se pretvoriti u zmijski otrov.
items.q: A student got a big portion of rice and fears a friend's lecture. A Persian expression kept word for word: can you guess its meaning?

items.text: – Zove se Quchan Bazaar i naša kuća je na kraju Quchan Bazaara.
items.q: Two boys argue about what their street is called. Does 'Quchan Bazaar' read naturally as its name?
before: Taj dan Hashem se posvađao s Abolfazlom. Abolfazl je rekao:

items.text: Khe, khe. Vukao si nas amo-tamo.
items.q: Does 'Vukao si nas amo-tamo' mean you wore us out?
before: – ...khe. Da. Ti nas nikad nisi vodio na takva mjesta. Uvijek groblje i bog zna što —crkva.

items.text: Tek kad sam se, na silu obitelji, pomiješao s kokošima, shvatio sam kakav je to drugačiji svijet na onoj strani priče.
items.q: A friend talks about his own life after his family pushed him. A Persian expression kept word for word: can you guess its meaning?

items.text: Za norouz stolom, u trenutku dolaska nove godine, kad sam čitao pjesmu za majku, Maman je umjesto da se raduje postala uznemirena.
items.q: At the Persian spring festival table, he read the poem exactly as the year turned. Is that moment clear?

items.text: Uvjeren da će mi odgovoriti, nazvah Maman i rekoh da su nam organizirali dopunsku nastavu pa moram ostati duže.
items.q: His made-up excuse is extra classes. Does 'dopunsku nastavu' mean that?

items.text: Srce mi je vedro pri pomisli da ćemo jednog dana sjediti jedno nasuprot drugome u kafiću, za stolom, kraj prozora, i dok kiša nježno sjeda na staklo, čitat ću joj priču, a ona će slušati sa zadovoljnim osmijehom.
items.q: Amir imagines reading his story to Niloofar in a cafe. Does this read naturally?

items.text: Maman je bacila moj madrac na vrh dvorišnog zida.
items.q: Maman simply put his mattress on top of the wall, without anger. Does 'bacila' say that?
